claims.author: A
claims.text: Taking the final PostgreSQL dump and uploads archive with containers still running but triggers disabled (before stop/freeze) yields a consistent snapshot, so the 027→028→029 ordering is correct, not a mistake.
claims.evidence: TASK-028 explicitly dumps 'with triggers disabled and containers still running'; pg_dump is transactionally consistent.
claims.test: Confirm the dump tool used is a transactional pg_dump and that no writer processes remain after trigger disable.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Not pre-creating 'tetsuo' and using a throwaway migration-admin avoids UID/home collisions when Migration Assistant recreates the account, directly serving GOAL-006.
claims.evidence: TASK-034 'create migration-admin; do not create tetsuo'; TASK-037 imports the complete tetsuo account.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Quarantining ~/Library/LaunchAgents and runtime caches before first interactive login (Phase 7) is the correct mechanism to satisfy GOAL-007 by preventing copied jobs from starting.
claims.evidence: TASK-039 moves LaunchAgents atomically before login; TASK-038 says 'Do not log into tetsuo yet'.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Keeping CrowdStrike/Jamf/Cisco/firewall enabled (TASK-035) can conflict with Migration Assistant pairing/transfer ports (TASK-036-038); the plan lacks a detect-and-reconcile step, risking a stall.
claims.evidence: TASK-035 forbids auto-disabling the firewall/endpoint agents; TASK-036 requires MA pairing and TASK-038 a 'verified fastest link'.
claims.test: Verify MA over Thunderbolt bridge is unaffected by the app firewall/EDR; if network discovery is needed, define an allow rule or documented exception.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Auto-start quarantine is scoped to ~/Library/LaunchAgents only; user login items (SMAppService/LoginItems) and other per-user start hooks are not named and may still auto-launch.
claims.evidence: TASK-039 addresses only LaunchAgents; no task enumerates login items.
claims.test: Enumerate SMAppService-registered login items in the migrated account and confirm none launch before dependency rebuild.

claims.author: A
claims.text: The pre-login validation gate (TASK-042) defines stop conditions but no rollback/recovery branch, leaving failure handling undefined.
claims.evidence: TASK-042 says 'Stop if ... any critical checksum differs' with no documented next action.
claims.test: Add an explicit failure path (retain migration-admin, preserve quarantine, re-run from encrypted kit).

claims.author: A
claims.text: Installing all macOS updates on the M5 before migrating (TASK-034) assumes destination version >= source version; this is unstated and can enlarge the incompatible-items list at TASK-038.
claims.evidence: TASK-034 'install all available macOS updates'; TASK-038 'record every incompatible or skipped item'.
claims.test: Assert and record source and destination macOS versions before MA.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Every task in Phases 5-8 declares explicit dependencies, and TASK-042 gates on all three Phase 7 quarantine tasks before first login, giving a well-formed ordering DAG.
claims.evidence: Each TASK lists 'Dependencies:'; TASK-042 depends on TASK-039, TASK-040, TASK-041.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Setting the new LaunchAgents directory to mode 0700 (TASK-039) diverges from the typical macOS 0755 default; over-restriction is low-risk but should be deliberate and recorded.
claims.test: Confirm 0700 does not impede launchd loading of user agents post-rebuild.

claims.author: B
claims.text: TASK-029 omits persistent inhibition of the installed interval-driven binary watchdog; its restart path bypasses the maintenance marker.
claims.evidence: Executed python3 -B static inspection of multica-ctl arrays and installed watchdog plists/scripts. Output: SERVICES_START_ORDER: binary-watchdog=False, factory-watchdog=False; SERVICES_LONG_RUNNING: binary-watchdog=False, factory-watchdog=False; binary-watchdog: StartInterval=600, KeepAlive=False, maintenance references=0; 84: if FORCE=1 "$HOME/.multica/bin/multica-ctl" restart >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then. read(multica-ctl,201..220) shows load_one uses launchctl load -w; read(370..394) shows restart calls cmd_stop then cmd_start.
claims.test: Compare every installed scheduled Multica label against persistent inhibition coverage. Static exclusion confirmed; falsify operational exposure with read-only exported override evidence proving binary-watchdog is disabled throughout transfer. Executing restart or launchctl is prohibited here.

history.note: Responds to A10: interval jobs are not covered by the controller's long-running classification. No restart occurrence asserted.

claims.author: B
claims.text: TASK-028 does not establish a writer barrier: an independent factory-watchdog sweep can mutate issues and rerun work after registered triggers are disabled.
claims.evidence: Executed python3 -B static inspection. Output: factory-watchdog: StartInterval=900, KeepAlive=False, maintenance references=0; 377: sweep_out="$("$HOMEDIR/.multica/bin/multica-orphan-sweep" --all 2>&1 | tail -1)"; orphan-sweep: trigger references=0, maintenance references=0; 122: elif multica --workspace-id "$ws" issue label add "$id" "$label_id" >/dev/null 2>&1; then; 135: if multica --workspace-id "$ws" issue rerun "$id" >/dev/null 2>&1; then. Complete read of sourced lib/multica-env.sh revealed constants/helpers, no inhibition gate.
claims.test: Before TASK-028, verify persistent watchdog inhibition and drain queued/in-flight writers; maintain blocked write ingress across both captures. Static independent writer path confirmed; live mutation testing is prohibited.

history.note: Responds to A1 and A10: TASK-029 verification is too late to protect TASK-028. Actual snapshot corruption is not asserted.

Executed lsof -p 96685 -Fn with runtime/disk filter: n/Users/tetsuo/Library/Application Support/rancher-desktop/lima/0/basedisk; n/Users/tetsuo/Library/Application Support/rancher-desktop/lima/0/diffdisk. Static seed scan: rancher lines: [36]; Lima lines: []; QEMU lines: [].

history.note: Adds machine evidence supporting A11. The disk-handle probe was inconclusive; current runtime presence does not prove future backup corruption.

claims.author: A
claims.text: B1/B2 now name a specific agent 'ai.multica.binary-watchdog' and a 'factory-watchdog sweep', neither of which (nor any watchdog entity) appears in the seed; they require it to be simultaneously not a 'registered trigger' (TASK-027) and not a 'long-running Multica label' (TASK-029). B named no refutedPremise against A10, so it stands and B1/B2 should be ASSUMPTION-grade.
claims.evidence: Seed strings: 'every registered trigger reports disabled'; 'Verify all long-running Multica labels are stopped/disabled'. No 'watchdog' token exists anywhere in the seed.
claims.test: Identify an actual inhibition path covering these interval jobs before TASK-028. Their absence from seed vocabulary does not negate installed executable behavior; TASK-029 coverage cannot retroactively protect TASK-028.

history.note: No assertion that the jobs must be excluded from every possible interpretation of 'long-running'; the supplied controller implementation excludes them.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Conceding B3's core gap: no Phase-5 task shuts down a source Rancher Desktop/Lima/QEMU VM (TASK-025 lists only VMware guests, TASK-031 quits only VMware Fusion, TASK-040 acts on the destination). claims.author: A
claims.text: TASK-031's explicit prohibition on evicting, hydrating, renaming, or recursively copying File Provider content is a correct safeguard that prevents mass-hydration/corruption of online-only cloud placeholders while still achieving GOAL-005 quiescence.

claims.test: Observe provider completion and post-quit activity, then compare placeholder/materialization state and recoverability before and after Migration Assistant; prohibition alone does not establish those results.
